messages:
maria: starting a small canary tonight for a p95-driven token trimming heuristic on conversation routes. goal: keep p95 <= 220ms while lowering average tokens by ~12-18%.

adam: share the canary plan + config? want to eyeball the guardrails. :eyes: 

maria: plan = 10% traffic in eu-west pool, tiered token budgets {low:48, med:64, high:96}. enable an early cutoff when queue_time > 8ms and batch_size >= 3. rollback triggers: p95 > baseline * 1.05 or errors > 0.5%.

zheng: is trimming KV-aware or naive prefix drop? curious about interactions with the KV cache hit behavior.

maria: KV-aware. logic: if kv_hit_rate(route) >= 0.7 -> no trim. 0.4<=kv_hit_rate<0.7 -> trim 10%. kv_hit_rate < 0.4 -> trim 25% and prefer the lighter kernel. config snippet below.

```
canary:
  traffic_pct: 10
  budgets:
    low: 48
    med: 64
    high: 96
  kv_gating:
    high_hit: 0.7
    med_hit: 0.4
  trim_factors:
    high_hit: 0.0
    med_hit: 0.1
    low_hit: 0.25
  early_cutoff:
    queue_ms: 8
    min_batch: 3
  rollout:
    ramp: [10, 30]
    ramp_window_mins: 120
  rollback:
    p95_rel_increase_pct: 5
    error_rate_pct: 0.5
```

ana: last time a kernel switch cost us a short-seq tail regression. do we have profiling comparing kernels when KV hits are low?

maria: yes. micro-profiling on canary instances shows that when effective tokens-per-request < 2.5, the default fused kernel gives worse p95 than kernel_b. heuristic: if est_batch_tokens_per_req < 2 AND kv_hit_rate < 0.5 -> prefer kernel_b at batch-formation. we switch kernels per-batch formation, not per-token, so overhead is tiny.

taylor: what about host CPU/memory churn when we flip kernels on the fly? we should monitor memcopy and prefetch counts.

maria: observed ~1% CPU bump on canary hosts, memcopy ops down with the KV prefetch gate. added metrics for mem_prefetch_ops and kernel_switch_count.

adam: saw any regressions during smoke tests?

maria: one regression on a bursty long-seq route (>1024 tokens). its kv_hit_rate oscillated 0.8->0.35 during the run and aggressive trim + kernel swap bumped p95 ~12%.

zheng: suggest a long-seq override: if avg_seq_len(route) > 512 then cap trim to 8% and avoid kernel switch unless est_batch_size < 1.5. prevents extra generation steps on long tails.

maria: agreed, adding long-seq override and lowering aggressiveness for routes with high sequence variance. also extending ramp: 10% -> 30% over 2h if p95 stays within 3% of baseline.

ana: observability checklist?

taylor: emit tags: route_id, kv_hit_bucket (high/med/low), kernel_choice, trimmed_tokens, avg_seq_len. dashboards: p95 by route, trimmed_tokens pct, mem_prefetch_ops, kernel_switch_count. alert: p95 delta > 4% sustained over 15m for the canary pool.

maria: added metrics and alert rules. will post canary summary in #eng-runtime after 3h window. thanks! :thumbsup: 

auto-deploy-bot: deploy job started: canary-config:slo-token-trimmer-2026-03-18

maria: deploy finished on canary pool. dashboards wired up and smoke checks passed. monitoring now collecting 15m rolling windows.
